subject.title: [Feature]: Support configurable request labels for Gemini API calls (GCP billing tracking)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Google/Vertex request labels as a public provider config surface, and what schema, provider scope, and privacy/cardinality limits should it use?
rationale: This adds provider-specific billing metadata to outbound model calls and expands the public config surface, so code alone cannot choose the permanent operator contract.

options.title: Approve bounded Vertex labels
options.body: Expose a validated Google/Vertex label map in the Google plugin, likely limited to Vertex-supported requests and documented GCP label constraints.

options.title: Use existing generic knobs
options.body: Decline a first-class field and ask operators to use existing headers/params/proxy paths only if those can satisfy billing attribution safely.

options.title: Defer provider metadata
options.body: Keep the issue open as product backlog until Google provider billing metadata has a broader cross-provider design.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded Vertex labels
recommendation.body: Expose a validated Google/Vertex label map in the Google plugin, likely limited to Vertex-supported requests and documented GCP label constraints.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership of the provider schema and Google transport surface makes this the best available routing candidate.
